data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A single large service with high internal redundancy is more resilient because decentralized networks are prone to 'cascading failures' via complex inter-service dependencies.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The large service lacks internal bulkheading, allowing a single bug to crash the entire process space.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decentralized network utilizes asynchronous, loosely coupled communication (e.g., event-driven architecture) that prevents backpressure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Tightly coupled failure propagation: In a decentralized network, services depend on one another through network calls. A failure in one small service can create backpressure or timeout loops that propagate to others, turning a local failure into a systemic collapse. A large service manages internal state and resource allocation centrally, allowing for more efficient 'circuit breaking' and global load shedding that prevents the system from entering a death spiral.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
